conviction_note: Two forces of similar size cancel. Q3 should land inside the $2.50-3.50 guide, probably above the $2.59 consensus, because Delta's primary release shows 15% TRASM and ex-refinery fuel of about $3.74 against UAL's $3.69 assumption. The Q4/FY guide, which is what the stock trades on, is built on a fuel curve about 7% higher in Brent than the one Delta used on Oct 2, with no refinery offset. The stock is already -14.5% over 20 days and -31% from its high, and the skew is balanced, so p_up 48 on abs 6.0 gives -0.24. impact_sum is 0.0 (pre-lessons +0.1), the same near-zero read.
bar: Q3 adjusted EPS consensus $2.59 on revenue $17.89B (GuruFocus Oct 16: https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9127579/united-airlines-q3-earnings-on-deck-what-to-expect ; MarketBeat same; Investing.com Oct 20 says $2.58/$17.89B: https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/united-airlines-faces-earnings-test-as-fuel-costs-squeeze-margins-93CH-4960455). Two sources agree. Company Q3 guide $2.50-3.50 at an all-in fuel price of $3.69/gal. FY2026 guide $9-11 against a $7.94 consensus, implying Q4 consensus of about $2.17 (H1 actual $3.18) (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000100517/000010051726000135/ual_erx06302026xex992.htm). TipRanks $3.19 and Yahoo $3.03 are outliers or a different basis and are rejected.
positioning_check: Short interest 16.8M shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 4.2 days to cover, down from 23.5M (5.4 DTC) on 2026-07-31; about 5.2% of shares outstanding (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/ual/short-interest/). Not crowded and being covered. Baseline: 25-delta skew -1.54 vol points (calls slightly richer than puts), put/call OI 0.55, priced_direction_lean 'balanced', event-implied move 5.44%, ATM IV 72%. Run-up -14.47% over 20 days and -4.55% over 5; 27.6% below the 52-week high. Sell-side: 24 of 28 Buy, 25 firms recently cut targets, and EPS estimates are down about 19% over 60 days but 'stabilized in past week' (Investing.com Oct 20).

findings.finding: Delta's Oct 9 release (a primary document published after UAL last spoke on Jul 15) shows Q3 TRASM +15% (3 points faster than Q2), transatlantic unit revenue +11%, premium revenue +18% and corporate sales up double digits. Its Q3 fuel was $3.61/gal including a 13c refinery benefit, so about $3.74 ex-refinery. UAL guided Q3 to $2.50-3.50 on $3.69 all-in fuel and TRASM above Q2's +12.1%. Read through, UAL's Q3 fuel overrun is small (about 5-15c/gal, roughly $0.15-0.45 of EPS) and its unit revenue likely beats its own floor, which points to Q3 EPS near $2.70-3.00 against a $2.59 consensus at the bottom of the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: UAL has beaten EPS estimates in 11 of its last 12 quarters and the stock rose after only 5 of them (investwithcolby substack, Oct 18). The Jul 15 print beat ($1.99 vs $1.88) with a reaffirmed guide and went -1.79%; Apr 21 went -5.58% on a guide cut despite a Q1 beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus $2.59 sits $0.09 above the low end of a $1.00-wide guide after a 19% cut in 60 days. If the market had taken in Delta's fuel and TRASM, Q3 consensus would sit nearer the midpoint. Revenue consensus (+17.5% YoY) already implies about 15% TRASM, so the upside is in fuel and cost, not revenue. The stock does not reward this line, so the reaction value is small.
findings.independence: UAL's own Jul 15 investor update (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000100517/000010051726000135/ual_erx06302026xex992.htm) gives the $3.69 assumption and TRASM above 12.1%. EIA weekly Gulf Coast jet averaged about $3.80 spot over Q3 (https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=EER_EPJK_PF4_RGC_DPG&f=W), slightly higher than Delta's realised price, which cuts against part of this. Delta itself missed its consensus ($1.72 vs $1.81).

findings.finding: Fuel for the Q4 guide is well above every earlier assumption. Gulf Coast jet spot ran $4.35-4.58 through Sep 4-Oct 9 against UAL's Jul 14 curve ($3.69 all-in for Q3). Delta's Q4 $4.25/gal is on the Oct 2 curve and includes a $0.40 refinery benefit UAL does not have, so it is about $4.65 for a non-refiner. Brent rose from $102.25 (Oct 2) to $109.55 (Oct 19), about another 20c/gal. American said on Sep 16 that Q4 fuel was about $1B above its July assumption. A UAL Q4 guide on the current curve likely implies FY EPS at or below the $7.94 consensus (Q4 about $2.17), against the $9-11 still on the books.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide cuts on fuel: Apr 21, 2026 (FY $12-14 cut to $7-11) went -5.58%. Oct 15, 2025 went -5.63%. Delta's FY cut on Oct 9, 2026 (to $5.10-5.60 from $6.50-7.50, Q4 below consensus) drew about -3% intraday (rttnews) and closed flat (82.14 to 82.17). UAL was also flat that day (107.44 to 107.46).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. UAL fell from $107.46 to $95.60 (Oct 9-19) while Brent rose from $104.7 to $109.6. But Investing.com says EPS estimates 'stabilized in the past week' while Brent made a new high on Oct 16, and the $7.94 FY consensus was printed by Oct 16. So a guide on the Oct 19 curve can read as a miss on the headline even though the stock has moved. If this were fully priced, consensus would have kept falling with oil and the stock would not have bounced +3% today.
findings.independence: Delta Q4 guide footnote (https://news.delta.com/sites/default/files/2026-10/delta-air-lines-announces-september-quarter-2026-results.pdf). Brent daily closes (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/BZ=F?range=1mo&interval=1d). American's Sep 16 $1B Q4 fuel comment, secondary (https://www.indmoney.com/blog/us-stocks/us-airlines-cut-flights-jet-fuel-costs-aal-ual-luv-stocks). findings.finding: Q4 revenue strength offsets part of the fuel hit. United executives said on Sep 16 that Q4 bookings 'remain very strong' with no broad demand destruction, while cutting some December flights. Delta guided Q4 total revenue about +20% YoY with sequential unit revenue improvement in both domestic and international. UAL's Q4 2025 comp is easy: RASM -1.6% and a $250M government-shutdown hit (Q4 2025 EPS $3.10).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jan 20, 2026: a revenue-momentum commentary with a strong guide went +2.2%. On fuel-shock prints, demand commentary has not stopped guide-driven declines (Apr 21 -5.58%).
findings.why_not_priced: Q4 consensus of about $2.17 is 30% below a Q4 2025 that carried a $0.60-ish shutdown hit. A street that had folded in 20% revenue growth on a 2%-capped capacity plan would not be this far below the prior year. The stock's 11% slide since Oct 9 has tracked oil, not demand.
findings.independence: Delta Q4 revenue guide (https://news.delta.com/sites/default/files/2026-10/delta-air-lines-announces-september-quarter-2026-results.pdf). UAL Q4 2025 shutdown hit (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/united-airlines-q4-earnings-call-highlights-2026-01-21/). The UAL Sep 16 statement comes only from a secondary blog.

findings.finding: Reaction analog: Delta cut FY EPS about 25% at the midpoint and guided Q4 below consensus on Oct 9, while showing record revenue. DAL traded about -3% in the morning and closed flat on the day (82.14 to 82.17), and UAL closed flat too (107.44 to 107.46). A fuel-driven guide cut with strong demand was not punished on print day; the later declines came with Brent.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Peer analog only. UAL's own guide-cut prints went -5.58% (Apr 2026) and -5.63% (Oct 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: This is a statement about the reaction function, not a fact the market lacks. It argues that a guide cut the sell-side has already modelled (FY consensus 7.94 vs a 9-11 guide) need not move the stock much on its own.
findings.independence: rttnews Oct 9 intraday -3% (https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx). This is a proxy; it rests partly on the Delta release shared with findings 1-3.

findings.finding: Expectations and positioning are already reset into the print. The stock is -14.5% over 20 days, -31% from its $138.77 high and at 9x trailing. FY consensus of $7.94 is $1.06 below the bottom of the company's guide. Short interest fell from 23.5M to 16.8M shares (Jul 31 to Sep 30, 4.2 days to cover). findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In the baseline's eight prints, the large up move (+14.33%, Jul 2025) came after a drawdown. The large down moves (-5.58, -5.63) came on guide cuts.
findings.why_not_priced: This is mostly priced by definition, and the 20-day run-up is the free control. The small positive rests on the market not paying for downside (negative skew, call-heavy OI) despite a guide cut being a near-certainty. A market braced for worse than consensus would show positive skew.
findings.independence: Baseline skew and OI (sealed file). Consensus and target cuts (https://investwithcolby.substack.com/p/ual-united-airlines-is-31-off-its).

findings.finding: Industry data show U.S. passenger traffic fell 3.3% YoY in Q3 while fares rose: volumes are weak and yield carries revenue. This is consistent with UAL capping Q3/Q4 capacity at +2% YoY and adding $10 to domestic one-way fares.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No company-specific reaction to traffic data is on record.
findings.why_not_priced: It is in today's wire copy and Delta has already shown revenue +16% on flat capacity, so it is mostly priced. It is an industry proxy that a broader, company-level series (Delta TRASM) partly contradicts.
findings.independence: The Delta release shows flat capacity and Main Cabin seats down while revenue rose, which explains the traffic decline as supply-driven (shared document).

lessons_applied: Rule 1 and rule 6 ('inside what the company guided'): the Q3 beat finding was cut from +0.8 to +0.4, because Q3 lands inside the $2.50-3.50 guide on a name that rose after only 5 of 12 beats
Rule 5 (proxy vs company number): the fuel-to-Q4-guide finding was trimmed from -1.8 to -1.5, because it is macro transmission confirmed only by peers (Delta, American), not by UAL
Rule 5: the Delta reaction analog was trimmed from +0.4 to +0.3 as a proxy
Rule 7: positioning was trimmed from +0.5 to +0.4, since short interest is low and skew near flat; there is no squeeze mechanism, only an absence of bid downside
Rule 3: the insider-sales finding was cut from -0.2 to -0.1, because its own caveat (routine sales at higher prices) argues against it
Rule 5: the industry traffic finding was cut from -0.2 to -0.1, because Delta's broader company-level TRASM series partly contradicts it
